questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the cell wall?

options.text: Protecting the cell from mechanical damage

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Synthesising proteins for the cell**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell wall** is a **non-living**, **rigid structure** that forms an outer covering for the **plasma membrane** in **plants**, **fungi**, **bacteria**, and **algae**.
 
• One of its primary roles is **providing shape to the cell**, which ensures the structural integrity of the plant or fungus and maintains its overall form. ***Hence, statement 1 is a correct function of the cell wall.***
 
• The cell wall facilitates **cell-to-cell interaction** through specialized channels called **plasmodesmata**, which traverse the cell walls to connect the **cytoplasm** of adjacent cells for communication and transport. ***Hence, statement 2 is a correct function of the cell wall.***
 
• The process of **synthesising proteins** is the function of **ribosomes**, which are located in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **rough endoplasmic reticulum**. The cell wall does not contain the machinery required for **protein synthesis**. ***Hence, statement 3 is NOT a function of the cell wall.***
 
• It acts as a formidable barrier, **protecting the cell from mechanical damage**, physical stress, and **infection** by various **pathogens**. ***Hence, statement 4 is a correct function of the cell wall.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Synthesising proteins for the cell.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Composition:**
 
 
• In **plants**, the cell wall is primarily composed of **cellulose**, **hemicellulose**, **pectins**, and **lignin**.
 
• **Algae** have cell walls made of **cellulose**, **galactans**, **mannans**, and minerals like **calcium carbonate**.
 
• In **fungi**, the cell wall is characterized by the presence of **chitin**, a durable **polysaccharide**.
 
 
 
• **Structural Layers:**
 
 
• The **primary cell wall** is thin and flexible, allowing for **cell growth** in young plants.
 
• The **secondary cell wall** is formed inside the primary wall once the cell is fully grown, providing extra **rigidity** and strength.
 
• The **middle lamella** is a layer rich in **calcium pectate** that acts as "glue" to hold neighboring cells together.
 
 
 
• **Permeability:** Unlike the **plasma membrane**, which is **selectively permeable**, the cell wall is generally **completely permeable** to water, oxygen, and other small solutes, allowing them to pass through freely.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Turgor Pressure:** The cell wall plays a critical role in resisting **turgor pressure**. This pressure is created when water enters the cell by **osmosis**; the rigid wall prevents the cell from **bursting** (lysis).
 
• **Bacterial Walls:** Most **bacteria** possess a cell wall made of **peptidoglycan** (murein). This is a target for many **antibiotics** like **penicillin**, which inhibit the cross-linking of the wall, leading to cell death.
 
• **Evolutionary Aspect:** The presence of a cell wall is a major distinguishing feature between **Plant cells** and **Animal cells**, as animal cells completely lack a cell wall.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following compounds would have the highest pH when dissolved in water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium hydroxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, commonly known as **caustic soda**, is a highly **alkaline** inorganic compound. When dissolved in **water**, it completely dissociates into **sodium ions (Na⁺)** and **hydroxide ions (OH⁻)**, making it a **strong base**.
 
• The **pH scale** is used to specify the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution. It ranges from **0 to 14**. A **pH of 7** is considered **neutral** (like pure water), a **pH below 7** is **acidic**, and a **pH above 7** is **basic**.
 
• **Sodium hydroxide** solutions typically exhibit a **pH** near **14** (for a **1M solution**), which is the highest possible value on the standard scale. ***Hence, the option regarding Sodium hydroxide is correct.***
 
• **Hydrogen chloride (HCl) gas**, when dissolved in water, forms **hydrochloric acid**, which is a **strong mineral acid**. It has a very **low pH**, often reaching **0 or 1**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Vinegar** is a solution containing **acetic acid (CH₃COOH)**. It is a **weak acid** with a typical **pH** value ranging between **2.4 and 3.0**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Lemon juice** contains a high concentration of **citric acid**. It is also a **weak acid** with a **pH** usually between **2 and 3**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The pH Concept**:
 
 
• The term **pH** stands for "**potential of Hydrogen**." It was first introduced by Danish biochemist **S.P.L. Sørensen** in **1909**.
 
• It is a **logarithmic scale**, meaning that each unit change in pH represents a **tenfold change** in **hydrogen ion concentration**. For example, a solution with **pH 4** is **10 times** more acidic than a solution with **pH 5**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Bases (Alkalis)**:
 
 
• Bases have a **bitter taste** and a **slippery or soapy feel** to the touch.
 
• They turn **red litmus paper blue** and react with acids to form **salt and water** in a **neutralization reaction**.
 
• Strong bases like **NaOH** and **Potassium hydroxide (KOH)** are highly **corrosive** and can cause severe chemical burns.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sodium Hydroxide**:
 
 
• **Industrial uses**: It is used in the manufacture of **soaps, detergents, paper, and textiles (rayon)**.
 
• **Chemical processing**: It is used in **petroleum refining** and as a **drain cleaner** because of its ability to dissolve greases and fats.

• **Relationship between pOH and pH**: In any aqueous solution at **25°C**, the sum of **pH and pOH** is always **14**. Since **Sodium hydroxide** provides a high concentration of **OH⁻ ions**, its **pOH** is very low (near 0), resulting in a **pH near 14**.
 
• **Common pH values**:
 
 
• **Battery Acid**: pH ~0.5
 
• **Stomach Acid**: pH ~1.5 - 3.5
 
• **Human Blood**: pH ~7.35 - 7.45 (slightly basic)
 
• **Milk of Magnesia**: pH ~10.5

questions.question:
In the given reaction, which of the following reactants has undergone oxidation?

 {PbO} + {H}₂ rightarrow {Pb} + {H}₂{O}
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The provided chemical equation **PbO + H2 → Pb + H2O** represents a **Redox reaction** (Reduction-Oxidation), where one reactant is oxidized and the other is reduced simultaneously.
 
• In this reaction, **Hydrogen (H2)** combines with **oxygen** to form **water (H2O)**. By definition, the **addition of oxygen** to a substance is called **oxidation**. Therefore, **H2** is the reactant that undergoes oxidation. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***
 
• **Lead(II) oxide (PbO)** loses its **oxygen** atom to become metallic **lead (Pb)**. The **removal of oxygen** from a substance is defined as **reduction**. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The substances **Pb** (Lead) and **H2O** (Water) are the **products** of the reaction. They are the result of the chemical change and are not the entities "undergoing" the reaction process as reactants. ***Hence, options 2 and 4 are incorrect.***
 
• Since **H2** is being oxidized, it serves as the **reducing agent** because it facilitates the reduction of **PbO** by removing its oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oxidation**: This chemical process involves the **gain of oxygen**, the **loss of hydrogen**, or the **loss of electrons** by an atom or molecule. In modern chemistry, it is primarily identified by an **increase in the oxidation state**.
 
• **Reduction**: This is the opposite of oxidation and involves the **loss of oxygen**, the **gain of hydrogen**, or the **gain of electrons**. It is characterized by a **decrease in the oxidation state**.
 
• **Oxidizing Agent**: This is a substance that causes the oxidation of another substance by accepting its electrons or providing oxygen. In this specific reaction, **PbO** acts as the **oxidizing agent**.
 
• **Reducing Agent**: This is a substance that causes the reduction of another substance by losing electrons or removing oxygen. In this reaction, **H2** acts as the **reducing agent**.
 
• **Reaction Characteristics**: This reaction typically occurs when **hydrogen gas** is passed over **heated lead oxide**. It is an important industrial and laboratory reaction used to demonstrate the **reactivity series** and the extraction of metals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Oxidation Number Analysis**: 
 
 
• The **oxidation state** of **Hydrogen (H)** in **H2** is **0** (elemental state), and it increases to **+1** in **H2O**. This **increase in oxidation number** confirms that oxidation has occurred.
 
• The **oxidation state** of **Lead (Pb)** in **PbO** is **+2**, and it decreases to **0** in the product **Pb**. This **decrease in oxidation number** confirms that reduction has occurred.
 
 
 
• **Electronic Concept**: While this reaction is easily explained via **oxygen transfer**, it also fits the **electronic concept** of redox where **Hydrogen** loses electrons (to oxygen) and **Lead** ions gain electrons to become neutral atoms.
 
• **State of Matter**: In a standard laboratory setting for this reaction, **PbO** is usually a **solid**, **H2** is a **gas**, **Pb** is a **solid**, and **H2O** is formed as **steam or liquid**.
</ul

questions.question: Which characteristic of parallel circuits makes them advantageous over series circuits for connecting multiple electrical gadgets in a house?

options.text: The total resistance is increased, protecting appliances.
The current is divided among the electrical gadgets, allowing them to operate independently.
If one component fails, the entire circuit is broken.
The potential difference across each gadget is unique.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The current is divided among the electrical gadgets, allowing them to operate independently.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the **electrical current** from the source is divided into multiple branches. This division allows each **electrical gadget** to draw the specific amount of **current** it requires to function correctly. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• One of the most significant advantages is **independent operation**. Since each appliance is connected across the same **potential difference** in its own separate branch, switching off or the failure of one appliance does not affect the operation of others.
 
• In household wiring, the **voltage** or **potential difference** remains constant across all gadgets. In countries like **India**, this standard domestic voltage is typically **220 Volts**. This ensures every device receives the full line voltage.
 
• Unlike series circuits, if a **bulb** or **fan** fuses in a parallel connection, the rest of the circuit remains intact, and other appliances continue to work normally. This makes it the preferred method for **domestic installations**.
 
• The **total effective resistance** in a parallel circuit **decreases** as more gadgets are added. This is because the inverse of the equivalent resistance is the sum of the inverses of individual resistances (**1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ...**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Series Circuits:**
 
 
• In a **series circuit**, there is only one path for the **current** to flow. If one component fails or is turned off, the **entire circuit is broken**, and no current flows to any other device.
 
• The **total resistance** in series is the sum of individual resistances (**Rs = R1 + R2 + ...**), which significantly reduces the current if many high-resistance gadgets are added.
 
 
 
• **Potential Difference (Voltage):**
 
 
• In **parallel**, the **potential difference** across every component is the **same**. In **series**, the total voltage is **divided** among the components based on their resistance.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• This fundamental principle states that **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance. This law governs how current distributes itself in the branches of a parallel circuit.
 
 
 
• **Safety Features:**
 
 
• While parallel circuits are advantageous, they can draw a high **total current** if too many appliances are used simultaneously. To prevent **overloading** and **short circuits**, safety devices like **fuses** or **Miniature Circuit Breakers (MCBs)** are installed in the main line.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Resistance Characteristic:** The claim that **total resistance increases** to protect appliances is incorrect for parallel circuits; resistance actually **decreases**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Failure Characteristic:** The idea that the **entire circuit breaks** if one component fails is a drawback of **series circuits**, not an advantage of parallel ones. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Voltage Characteristic:** In a parallel circuit, the **potential difference** is **identical** for all gadgets, not unique. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Application:** Because of these features, **parallel circuits** are used in **buildings**, **offices**, and **industrial plants** to ensure reliable and independent power distribution.
</ul

questions.question: A person shows high blood sugar levels even after eating small amounts of food. What may be the cause?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lack of insulin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• High blood sugar levels, medically termed **hyperglycemia**, occur when the body cannot effectively transport glucose from the bloodstream into the cells for energy.
 
• **Insulin** is a hormone produced by the **beta cells** of the **Islets of Langerhans** in the **pancreas**. Its primary role is to regulate **blood glucose levels**.
 
• After consuming food, blood sugar levels rise. In a healthy individual, the **pancreas** releases **insulin**, which acts like a "key" to unlock cells, allowing **glucose** to enter.
 
• A **lack of insulin** or a deficiency in its secretion means glucose remains in the blood even after small amounts of food are consumed, leading to elevated sugar levels. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• This condition is the hallmark of **Diabetes Mellitus**, specifically **Type 1 Diabetes** (where insulin production is absent) or **Type 2 Diabetes** (where the body becomes resistant or produces insufficient insulin).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Excess Growth Hormone:**
 
 
• **Growth Hormone (Somatotropin)** is secreted by the **anterior pituitary gland**.
 
• While it can have "diabetogenic" effects (antagonizing insulin) if present in massive excess, its primary role is **physical growth**, **cell reproduction**, and **regeneration**.
 
• Excessive secretion in adults leads to **Acromegaly** and in children leads to **Gigantism**.
 
 
 
• **Excess Estrogen:**
 
 
• **Estrogen** is the primary female sex hormone produced mainly by the **ovaries**.
 
• It is responsible for the development of **secondary sexual characteristics** and the regulation of the **menstrual cycle** and **reproductive system**.
 
• It does not directly cause high blood sugar levels as its primary physiological function.
 
 
 
• **Low Thyroxine:**
 
 
• **Thyroxine (T4)** is produced by the **thyroid gland** and is essential for regulating the **Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)**.
 
• **Low thyroxine** (Hypothyroidism) leads to symptoms like weight gain, fatigue, and cold intolerance, rather than high blood sugar.
 
• Thyroid hormones generally increase the absorption of glucose from the gastrointestinal tract, but a deficiency does not cause hyperglycemia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Glucagon:** This is the antagonist to insulin, secreted by the **alpha cells** of the **pancreas**. It raises blood glucose levels by stimulating **glycogenolysis** (breakdown of glycogen) in the **liver**.
 
• **Normal Blood Sugar Levels:** For a healthy adult, fasting blood sugar is typically between **70 to 99 mg/dL**. Post-meal (postprandial) levels should ideally be less than **140 mg/dL** after **2 hours**.
 
• **Pancreas as a Dual Gland:** The **pancreas** is a **heterocrine gland**, meaning it has both **exocrine** functions (producing digestive enzymes like **trypsin** and **lipase**) and **endocrine** functions (secreting hormones like **insulin**, **glucagon**, and **somatostatin**).
 
• **Diabetes Symptoms:** Common indicators of chronic high blood sugar include **polyuria** (excessive urination), **polydipsia** (increased thirst), and **unexplained weight loss**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following mixtures is a suspension?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muddy water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **suspension** is defined as a **heterogeneous mixture** in which the **solute-like particles** do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the bulk of the solvent.
 
• **Muddy water** is a classic example of a suspension because it consists of **soil, sand, and clay particles** dispersed in **water**. These particles are large enough to be seen with the **naked eye**.
 
• The **particle size** in a suspension is typically **greater than 1000 nanometers** (or **1 micrometer**). Because of this large size, the particles are affected by **gravity** and will **settle down** at the bottom of the container if the mixture is left undisturbed for a period of time.
 
• Suspensions are **unstable** in nature. Unlike solutions, the components of a suspension like muddy water can be easily separated through physical methods such as **filtration** using **filter paper** or **decantation**.
 
• When a beam of light is passed through a fresh suspension, the large particles **scatter the light**, making the path of the beam visible. This phenomenon is known as the **Tyndall effect**. However, once the particles settle, the mixture no longer scatters light effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solutions (Homogeneous Mixtures):**
 
 
• **Salt water** and **Vinegar** (a mixture of **acetic acid** and water) are examples of **true solutions**.
 
• In a solution, the **solute particles** are smaller than **1 nanometer** in diameter, meaning they are distributed uniformly at the **molecular level** and cannot be seen even with a microscope.
 
• Solutions are highly **stable**, do not settle over time, and do not show the **Tyndall effect** because the particles are too small to scatter light.
 
 
 
• **Colloids:**
 
 
• **Milk** is a **colloid**, specifically a type of **emulsion** where liquid fat globules are dispersed in water.
 
• Colloidal particles have a size ranging between **1 nanometer and 1000 nanometers**. They are large enough to scatter light (showing the **Tyndall effect**) but small enough that they do not settle under **gravity**.
 
• Colloids appear **homogeneous** to the naked eye but are actually **heterogeneous** when viewed under an ultra-microscope.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Mixtures:**
 
 
• **Suspensions** are opaque or translucent, **Colloids** are often cloudy or milky, and **Solutions** are typically **transparent**.
 
• While **suspensions** can be separated by ordinary **filtration**, **colloids** require specialized techniques like **centrifugation** to separate the dispersed phase from the medium.
 
• Common examples of suspensions include **chalk powder in water**, **flour in water**, and **magnesia (milk of magnesia)**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: What will be the acceleration due to gravity on a planet whose mass and radius are double that of the Earth? (Take the acceleration due to gravity on Earth as g .)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**g/2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** on the surface of any planet or celestial body is determined by the formula **g = GM / R²**, where **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, **M** is the **mass** of the body, and **R** is its **radius**.
 
• In this problem, the new planet has a **mass (M')** that is **double** that of the **Earth**, which can be represented as **M' = 2M**.
 
• The **radius (R')** of the new planet is also **double** that of the **Earth**, represented as **R' = 2R**.
 
• By substituting these new values into the gravity formula, we get the new acceleration: **g' = G(2M) / (2R)²**. This simplifies to **g' = 2GM / 4R²**.

questions.question: In the absence of any external force, a moving body will _______.

options.text: Maintain a constant velocity in straight line
Slow down and change its path
Continue to move with constant acceleration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maintain a constant velocity in straight line**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, also known as the **Law of Inertia**, an object will remain at **rest** or continue to move at a **constant velocity** in a **straight line** unless acted upon by a **net external force**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Inertia** is the inherent property of an object to resist any change in its state of **motion** or **rest**. It is not a force that causes an object to stop; rather, it is the reason why an object keeps moving in the absence of resistance. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• When the **external force** is **zero**, the **acceleration** of the body must also be **zero** (based on **F = ma**). Constant acceleration would imply a continuous **force** is being applied. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• For a body to **slow down** or **change its path**, an external influence such as **friction**, **air resistance**, or **gravitational pull** must be present to change its **magnitude** or **direction** of velocity. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• In a vacuum or **deep space**, far from **gravitational fields** and **atmospheric friction**, a moving object will theoretically travel forever in the same **direction** and at the same **speed**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**
 
 
• These laws were first formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** and published in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in the year **1687**.
 
• **First Law (Inertia):** Defines the concept of **force** qualitatively. It explains that **motion** does not require a force to maintain it, but change in motion does.
 
• **Second Law (F=ma):** Provides a **quantitative measure** of force. It states that the **rate of change of momentum** of a body is directly proportional to the applied **force** and takes place in the direction in which the force acts.
 
• **Third Law (Action and Reaction):** States that for every **action**, there is an **equal and opposite reaction**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Inertia:**
 
 
• The **mass** of an object is a quantitative measure of its **inertia**. A larger **mass** requires more **force** to achieve the same **acceleration**.
 
• There are three types of inertia: **Inertia of Rest** (resistance to starting motion), **Inertia of Motion** (resistance to stopping), and **Inertia of Direction** (resistance to turning).
 
 
 
• **Galileo’s Contribution:**
 
 
• Before Newton, **Galileo Galilei** challenged the Aristotelian view that a force is required to keep an object moving. He used experiments with **frictionless inclined planes** to demonstrate that an object would move indefinitely if **friction** were eliminated.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Velocity vs. Speed:** In the context of **Newton's First Law**, "constant velocity" is a **vector quantity**, meaning both the **speed** (scalar) and the **direction** remain unchanged.
 
• **Net Force:** It is possible for multiple forces to act on a body, but if their **vector sum** is **zero**, the body is in **equilibrium** and will maintain its **velocity**. This is common in **terminal velocity** scenarios where **gravity** and **air resistance** are balanced.
 
• **External Force:** This refers to forces originating from outside the system, such as **pushing**, **pulling**, **friction**, or **magnetism**. **Internal forces** within a system cannot change the motion of the system's **center of mass**.
 
• **Inertial Frame of Reference:** Newton's Laws hold true in **Inertial frames**, which are frames that are not **accelerating** or **rotating** relative to the "fixed stars."

questions.question: Why is variation important in a population of organisms?

options.text: It causes extinction of all organisms.
It helps some individuals survive if environmental conditions change.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It helps some individuals survive if environmental conditions change.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Variation** refers to the differences in **DNA sequences** and phenotypic traits among individuals within a **population**. These differences are the foundation of **evolution** and **adaptation**.
 
• Variation is crucial because it ensures that some individuals in a **species** possess traits that allow them to survive **drastic environmental changes**, such as **global warming**, **new diseases**, or **famine**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Without variation, a **population** would be genetically identical. If a lethal **environmental stressor** occurred, every individual would be equally susceptible, potentially leading to **mass extinction**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Variation increases the diversity of a **population** rather than making them identical. Identity is a characteristic of **clones** produced via **asexual reproduction**, whereas **variation** is the opposite. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Variation does not prevent **reproduction**; instead, it is often a byproduct of it. Sexual reproduction involves **meiosis** and **genetic recombination**, which are the primary mechanisms that generate **new variations** in offspring. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sources of Variation:** Genetic variation arises from several sources, including **random mutations** in **DNA**, **gene flow** (the movement of genes between populations), and **sexual reproduction**, which shuffles alleles into new combinations.
 
• **Natural Selection:** Proposed by **Charles Darwin** in his **1859** work, "On the Origin of Species," **natural selection** acts on variation. Individuals with **advantageous traits** (variations) are more likely to **survive** and pass those traits to the next **generation**.
 
• **Genetic Diversity:** A high level of **genetic diversity** within a **species** provides a "biological insurance policy," allowing the population to persist through **fluctuating conditions** over **geological time**.
 
• **Example of Variation:** The **Peppered Moth** in the **United Kingdom** is a classic **textbook example**. Before the **Industrial Revolution**, light-colored moths were common. As pollution darkened tree trunks, the dark-colored **variant** survived better, illustrating how **variation** aids survival during **environmental shifts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mutation:** This is a permanent change in the **nucleotide sequence** of the **genome**. While most mutations are neutral, some provide the **beneficial variations** necessary for **survival**.
 
• **Niche Occupation:** Variation allows different individuals to occupy slightly different **ecological niches**, reducing **competition** within the same **population** and allowing for better **resource utilization**.
 
• **Species Persistence:** For long-term **species persistence**, variation is not just a benefit but a necessity. It is the primary tool used by **conservation biologists** to measure the health of **endangered species**.
</ul

questions.question: Which element is necessary for the thyroid gland to secrete the thyroxine hormone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iodine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iodine** is a vital trace element that the **thyroid gland** requires to synthesize **thyroid hormones**, specifically **thyroxine (T4)** and **triiodothyronine (T3)**.
 
• The **thyroid gland** is a butterfly-shaped endocrine organ located in the **neck**, just below the **Adam's apple**, and it plays a major role in regulating **metabolism**, **growth**, and **body temperature**.
 
• The synthesis process occurs when the thyroid gland takes up **iodide ions** from the blood and attaches them to the amino acid **tyrosine** within a large protein called **thyroglobulin**. *Hence, the statement that Iodine is necessary for thyroxine secretion is correct.*
 
• **Thyroxine (T4)** acts as a prohormone and is converted into the more active **triiodothyronine (T3)** in various tissues like the **liver** and **kidneys**.
 
• A deficiency of dietary iodine leads to the inability of the gland to produce sufficient hormones, which triggers the **pituitary gland** to release more **Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH)**, potentially leading to **Goitre** (enlargement of the thyroid).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Elements (Halogens):**
 
 
• **Fluorine (F):** It is essential for the health of **teeth** and **bones**. It helps in the prevention of **dental caries** by strengthening **enamel**, but it does not participate in the synthesis of thyroid hormones.
 
• **Bromine (Br):** While it is a **halogen** similar to iodine, it has no established role in the secretion of thyroxine. In fact, excessive **bromide** exposure can sometimes interfere with iodine uptake in the thyroid.
 
• **Chlorine (Cl):** It is an essential **electrolyte** found in the body as **chloride ions**. It is crucial for maintaining **osmotic pressure**, **acid-base balance**, and the production of **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** in the stomach, but it is not used by the thyroid gland for hormone production.
 
 
 
• **Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDD):**
 
 
• **Hypothyroidism:** A condition where the thyroid gland is underactive, leading to **fatigue**, **weight gain**, and **depression**.
 
• **Cretinism:** Severe iodine deficiency during **pregnancy** can lead to stunted physical and mental growth in the infant, a condition known as **congenital iodine deficiency syndrome**.
 
• **Goitre:** The characteristic **swelling of the neck** resulting from the enlargement of the thyroid gland due to iodine deficiency.
 
 
 
• **Sources of Iodine:**
 
 
• The most common source of iodine for humans is **iodized salt**, which was introduced as a public health measure in the **20th century**.
 
• Natural sources include **seafood** (fish, seaweed, shrimp), **dairy products**, and **eggs**. The amount of iodine in plants depends on the **iodine content of the soil** in which they are grown.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Function:** Thyroxine controls the **Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR)** and regulates the metabolism of **carbohydrates**, **proteins**, and **fats**.
 
• **Daily Requirement:** The recommended daily intake of iodine for an average **adult** is approximately **150 micrograms (mcg)**, which increases during **pregnancy** and **lactation**.
 
• **Global Context:** Iodine deficiency remains a significant public health issue in many parts of the world, particularly in **mountainous regions** where iodine has been leached from the soil by **glaciation** or **flooding**.
</ul

questions.question: Which part of the flower protects the ovule and later transforms into the fruit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ovary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ovary** is the basal, swollen part of the **carpel** or **pistil** (the female reproductive organ of a flower) that houses the **ovules**.
 
• One of its primary biological functions is to provide **protection** to the **ovules** from the external environment and potential pathogens during the developmental stage.
 
• After the process of **fertilization** occurs, the **ovary** undergoes significant physiological and structural changes, eventually maturing and ripening into a **fruit**.
 
• Inside the developing fruit, the **ovules** undergo their own transformation to become **seeds**, which contain the embryo for the next generation of the plant.
 
• The wall of the **ovary** develops into the **pericarp**, which is the part of the **fruit** that we often consume or that serves to disperse the **seeds**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Petals (Corolla):**
 
 
• **Petals** are typically the brightly colored, **pigmented** parts of a flower.
 
• Their main function is to **attract pollinators** such as **bees**, **butterflies**, and **birds** through visual appeal and sometimes **scent**.
 
• They also provide additional protection to the **reproductive organs** (stamen and pistil) located at the center of the flower.
 
 
 
• **Stigma:**
 
 
• The **Stigma** is the uppermost, often **sticky** or feathery tip of the **pistil**.
 
• It serves as the **receptive platform** where **pollen grains** land during the process of **pollination**.
 
• Once **pollen** adheres to the **stigma**, it germinates and grows a **pollen tube** down through the **style** to reach the **ovary**.
 
 
 
• **Sepals (Calyx):**
 
 
• **Sepals** are the outermost green, leaf-like structures that enclose the **flower bud** before it opens.
 
• They function primarily as **protection** for the delicate inner floral parts during the **bud stage** of development.
 
• In some species, **sepals** may persist after the flower opens to support the base of the **petals**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **True Fruits:** These are fruits that develop exclusively from a **ripened ovary**. Examples include **Mangoes**, **Grapes**, and **Blueberries**.
 
• **False Fruits:** In some plants, other floral parts like the **thalamus** or **receptacle** contribute to the formation of the fruit along with the **ovary**. Common examples include **Apples**, **Pears**, and **Strawberries**.
 
• **Pollination and Fertilization:** **Pollination** is the transfer of **pollen** from the **anther** to the **stigma**, whereas **fertilization** is the actual fusion of the male and female **gametes** inside the **ovule**.
 
• **Angiosperms:** This group of plants is characterized by having **flowers** and producing **seeds** enclosed within a **fruit**, a direct result of the **ovary's** development post-fertilization.
</ul

questions.question:

(A): Sound waves are transverse waves.

options.text: Both assertion and reason are false.

Assertion is false and reason is true.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound waves** are characterized as **longitudinal waves**, not transverse waves, because the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction in which the wave travels. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is false.***
 
• In a **longitudinal wave**, the displacement of the medium is in the same direction as, or the opposite direction to, the direction of propagation of the wave, creating regions of **compressions** and **rarefactions**.
 
• **Sound** is a **mechanical wave**, which means it requires a **material medium** such as **solid, liquid, or gas** for its propagation. ***Hence, Reason (R) is true.***
 
• The reason sound cannot travel through a **vacuum** (like outer space) is that there are no molecules to compress and expand to transmit the **vibrational energy**.
 
• While the reason statement is a factually correct scientific principle regarding the nature of sound, it does not explain why the assertion is true or false; however, since the assertion itself is factually incorrect, the relationship of "correct explanation" does not apply.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Transverse Waves:**
 
 
• In these waves, the particles of the medium move **perpendicular** to the direction of the wave's propagation.
 
• Examples include **light waves**, **radio waves**, and waves on a plucked **guitar string**.
 
• These waves consist of **crests** (highest points) and **troughs** (lowest points).
 
 
 
• **Longitudinal Waves:**
 
 
• These waves travel through a medium by causing particles to oscillate back and forth in the **same direction** as the wave.
 
• **Sound waves** in air and **ultrasound waves** are the most common examples.
 
• They are characterized by **compressions** (high-pressure zones) and **rarefactions** (low-pressure zones).
 
 
 
• **Medium of Propagation:**
 
 
• The **speed of sound** varies depending on the medium; it is **fastest in solids** (approx. **5000 m/s** in steel), slower in **liquids** (approx. **1500 m/s** in water), and slowest in **gases** (approx. **343 m/s** in air at **20 degrees Celsius**).
 
• This speed variation is due to the **density** and **elasticity** of the material.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mechanical vs. Electromagnetic Waves:**
 
 
• **Mechanical waves** (like sound and water waves) **require a medium** to transfer energy from one location to another.
 
• **Electromagnetic waves** (like visible light, X-rays, and Microwaves) can travel through a **vacuum** at the speed of **3 x 10⁸ m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Human Hearing Range:**
 
 
• The standard **audible frequency range** for humans is between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**.
 
• Frequencies below 20 Hz are called **infrasonic**, and those above 20,000 Hz are called **ultrasonic**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: If the velocity–time graph of an object is curved, it indicates ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-uniform acceleration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **velocity-time graph** (v-t graph) represents the relationship between the **velocity** of an object and the **time** elapsed. The **vertical axis** (y-axis) represents velocity, and the **horizontal axis** (x-axis) represents time.
 
• The **slope** or gradient of a velocity-time graph at any point represents the **acceleration** of the object. If the graph is a **straight line**, the slope is constant, implying **uniform acceleration**.
 
• If the velocity-time graph is **curved**, it indicates that the **slope is changing** at every point. Since the slope represents acceleration, a changing slope means the **acceleration is not constant**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Non-uniform acceleration.***
 
• **Constant speed** or **Uniform motion** would be represented by a **straight horizontal line** parallel to the time axis. In such a case, the velocity remains the same as time passes, and the acceleration is **zero**. ***Hence, options 1 and 2 are incorrect.***
 
• **Zero velocity** would be represented by a line coinciding with the **time axis** (where the value on the y-axis is **0**). A curve indicates that the velocity is changing, so it cannot be zero. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration**: It is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** with respect to **time**. The **SI unit** of acceleration is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it has both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• **Uniform vs. Non-Uniform Acceleration**:
 
 
• **Uniform Acceleration**: An object is said to be in uniform acceleration if its velocity increases or decreases by **equal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**. A classic example is an object in **free fall** under gravity, accelerating at approximately **9.8 m/s²**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Acceleration**: This occurs when the velocity of an object changes by **unequal amounts** in **equal intervals of time**. A car moving through **crowded city traffic** or a **bus** stopping at various stations typically exhibits non-uniform acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Area Under the Graph**: In a velocity-time graph, the **area** enclosed by the graph and the time axis represents the total **displacement** or **distance** traveled by the object during that **time interval**.
 
• **Instantaneous Acceleration**: For a **curved v-t graph**, the acceleration at a specific **instant** is called instantaneous acceleration. It is found by drawing a **tangent** to the curve at that particular **point in time** and calculating the slope of that tangent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Positive and Negative Slopes**: 
 
 
• A **positive slope** (line or curve going upwards) indicates that the object is **speeding up** (positive acceleration).
 
• A **negative slope** (line or curve going downwards) indicates that the object is **slowing down**, which is also known as **retardation** or **deceleration**.
 
 
 
• **Position-Time Graph Comparison**: It is important not to confuse v-t graphs with **position-time (s-t) graphs**. In an s-t graph, a **straight line** indicates **uniform velocity**, and a **curve** indicates **acceleration**.
 
• **Physical Significance**: The study of these graphs is a fundamental part of **kinematics**, used by **engineers** and **physicists** to analyze the motion of **vehicles**, **projectiles**, and **celestial bodies**.

• Successive members of such a series differ from each other by a **CH2** unit, which is also known as a **methylene group**.
 
• This structural difference implies that each consecutive member has **one carbon atom** and **two hydrogen atoms** more than the preceding member. ***Hence, the correct answer is One carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms.***
 
• Because of this **CH2** difference, the **molecular mass** of any two adjacent members in a homologous series differs by **14 atomic mass units (u)** (where **Carbon** is **12 u** and **Hydrogen** is **1 u**).
 
• The members of a homologous series can be represented by a **general molecular formula**, such as **CnH2n+2** for **alkanes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alkanes:** These are **saturated hydrocarbons** with the general formula **CnH2n+2**. For example, **Methane (CH4)** and **Ethane (C2H6)** differ by exactly **one carbon** and **two hydrogen atoms**.
 
• **Alkenes:** These are **unsaturated hydrocarbons** containing at least one **double bond**, represented by the formula **CnH2n**. Examples include **Ethene (C2H4)** and **Propene (C3H6)**.
 
• **Alkynes:** These are **unsaturated hydrocarbons** containing at least one **triple bond**, following the formula **CnH2n-2**. Examples include **Ethyne (C2H2)** and **Propyne (C3H4)**.
 
• **Physical Properties:** As the **molecular mass** increases within a homologous series, there is a regular **gradation** in physical properties. For instance, the **melting point** and **boiling point** increase as the number of carbon atoms increases due to stronger **intermolecular forces**.
 
• **Chemical Properties:** Since all members of a series have the same **functional group** (like the **-OH** group in **alcohols**), they exhibit very similar **chemical reactions** and **reactivity** patterns.
 
• **Solubility:** The **solubility** of members in a particular solvent (like **water**) often decreases as the **carbon chain length** increases within the series.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **General Formulae:** The ability to predict the formula of any member using **n** (the number of carbon atoms) is a hallmark of these series. For **Alcohols**, the formula is **CnH2n+1OH**.
 
• **Nomenclature:** The **IUPAC** naming system uses specific **suffixes** and **prefixes** based on the homologous series, such as **-ane** for alkanes, **-ene** for alkenes, and **-ol** for alcohols.
 
• **History:** The concept of **homology** was introduced in the **19th century** (around **1843**) by the French chemist **Charles Gerhardt** to classify organic substances.
 
• **Isomerism:** While members share a general formula, as the **number of carbon atoms** increases (usually from **n=4** onwards), the number of possible **structural isomers** also increases significantly.
</ul

questions.question: The atomic number of an element is equal to which of the following?

options.text: Number of neutrons + number of protons

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of protons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atomic Number**, represented by the symbol **Z**, is defined as the total **number of protons** present in the nucleus of an atom. This value uniquely identifies a chemical element. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **number of protons** determines the charge of the nucleus and the identity of the element. For example, any atom with **6 protons** is **Carbon**, and any atom with **11 protons** is **Sodium**.
 
• The **number of neutrons** can vary within atoms of the same element. These variations are known as **isotopes**. Since the neutron count can change while the element remains the same, the atomic number is not equal to the number of neutrons. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• In a **neutral atom**, the **number of electrons** is equal to the **atomic number** (protons) to maintain electrical neutrality. However, atoms can lose or gain electrons to form **ions**. Because the electron count changes during chemical reactions while the identity (protons) remains constant, the atomic number is fundamentally defined by protons, not electrons. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The sum of the **number of protons and neutrons** is referred to as the **Mass Number (A)**. This represents the approximate mass of the atom in atomic mass units. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Modern Periodic Law**: In **1913**, the scientist **Henry Moseley** used X-ray spectroscopy to show that the **atomic number (Z)** is the fundamental property of an element. This discovery replaced **Mendeleev’s** periodic law, which was based on atomic mass.
 
• **Periodic Table Arrangement**: The elements in the **Modern Periodic Table** are arranged in increasing order of their **atomic numbers**. This arrangement ensures that elements with similar electronic configurations and chemical properties fall into the same **group**.
 
• **Notation**: In chemical notation, the **atomic number (Z)** is usually written as a subscript to the left of the element symbol, while the **mass number (A)** is written as a superscript. For example, **Carbon-12** is represented with **6** as the subscript and **12** as the superscript.
 
• **Isotopes**: These are atoms with the **same atomic number** but **different mass numbers**. For instance, **Hydrogen** has three isotopes: **Protium** (1 proton, 0 neutrons), **Deuterium** (1 proton, 1 neutron), and **Tritium** (1 proton, 2 neutrons).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Protons**: These are **positively charged** subatomic particles located in the nucleus. The discovery of the nucleus is attributed to **Ernest Rutherford** following his famous **Gold Foil Experiment** in **1911**.
 
• **Neutrons**: These are **neutral** particles (no charge) discovered by **James Chadwick** in **1932**. The mass of a neutron is slightly greater than that of a proton.
 
• **Electrons**: These are **negatively charged** particles that revolve around the nucleus in specific orbits or shells. They were discovered by **J.J. Thomson** in **1897** through his **Cathode Ray Tube** experiments.
 
• **Nucleons**: This is a collective term for both **protons** and **neutrons**, as they are the particles that constitute the **nucleus** of an atom.
 
• **Isobars**: These are atoms of different elements (different **atomic numbers**) that have the **same mass number**. An example is **Argon-40** and **Calcium-40**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of negative work?

options.text: Friction acting on a moving object
Gravity acting on a falling ball

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Friction acting on a moving object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work Done** is defined as the product of the component of the **Force** in the direction of the displacement and the magnitude of this **Displacement**. It is represented by the formula **W = Fs cos θ**, where **F** is the force, **s** is the displacement, and **θ** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
• **Negative Work** occurs when the **Force** and the **Displacement** are in opposite directions, meaning the angle **θ** is **180 degrees**. Since **cos 180° = -1**, the work done becomes negative.
 
• **Lifting a bag upwards**: When a person lifts a bag, the applied **Force** is in the upward direction and the **Displacement** is also upward. Since both are in the same direction (**θ = 0°**), the work done by the person is **Positive**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Friction acting on a moving object**: **Friction** always acts in a direction **opposite** to the direction of motion or **Displacement** of the object. Because the angle between the frictional force and displacement is **180 degrees**, the work done by friction is always **Negative**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Gravity acting on a falling ball**: When a ball falls towards the earth, the force of **Gravity** acts downwards and the **Displacement** is also downwards. As the force and displacement are in the same direction, the work done by gravity is **Positive**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Pushing a moving car forward**: When you push a car in the same direction it is already moving, the **Force** applied and the **Displacement** occur in the same direction. This results in **Positive Work** being done on the car. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Friction acting on a moving object.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Work Done:**
 
 
• **Positive Work:** When the force and displacement are in the same direction (angle **θ** is between **0 and 90 degrees**). An example is a horse pulling a cart or a **Spring** being stretched.
 
• **Negative Work:** When the force and displacement are in opposite directions (angle **θ** is between **90 and 180 degrees**). This usually happens when a force **opposes** the motion, such as **Air Resistance** or **Braking** a vehicle.
 
• **Zero Work:** When the **Force** and **Displacement** are perpendicular (**θ = 90°**) or if either force or displacement is **zero**. For example, if a **Coolie** carries a load on his head and walks on a horizontal platform, the force of gravity is vertical while the displacement is horizontal, making the work done by gravity **zero**.
 
 
 
• **SI Unit and Nature:**
 
 
• The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, which is equivalent to **1 Newton-meter (N-m)**.
 
• **Work** is a **Scalar Quantity**, meaning it has only **magnitude** and no specific direction, even though it is calculated using vector quantities like force and displacement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Transfer:** **Positive Work** results in an **increase** in the energy of the system, while **Negative Work** results in a **decrease** or loss of energy from the system (often dissipated as **Heat**).
 
• **Dimensional Formula:** The dimensional formula for work is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is the same as the dimensional formula for **Energy** and **Torque**.
 
• **Application in Daily Life:** Understanding negative work is crucial in engineering, especially when designing **Braking Systems** in automobiles and **Safety Gear** that must absorb **Kinetic Energy** to bring objects to a stop.
